policy_title: Expand Free Childcare for Working Parents
stated: The Conservative Party will deliver the largest ever expansion of childcare, providing 30 hours of free childcare a week for working parents from when their child is nine months old until they start school by September 2025, saving eligible families an average of £6,900 per year.

source.quote: Give working parents 30 hours of free childcare a week from when their child is nine months old to when they start school, saving eligible families an average of £6,900 per year. ...From September 2025, all eligible parents with children from nine months old to when they start school will be able to access 30 hours of free childcare a week.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly reduces a major household expense (childcare) by an average of £6,900/year for eligible families, materially increasing real disposable income for working parents.

Subsidised childcare from 9 months removes a primary barrier to parental (especially maternal) workforce participation, affecting employment rates, hours worked, and in-work poverty for families with young children.

30 hours of early years provision constitutes early years education, which evidence links to school readiness and the attainment gap; the working-parent-only eligibility condition is a real tension that could widen the attainment gap for children of non-working (often lower-income) households — a genuine O7 verdict.

The scale of the commitment (extending 30-hour entitlement to under-2s across England) represents a multi-billion-pound recurring spending obligation; adequacy of the funding rate to providers is a live fiscal-sustainability question.

Expanding affordable childcare is strongly associated in the literature with increased female labour force participation and aggregate labour supply, raising productivity and real living standards at the macro level.

Entitlement conditioned on parental employment means the largest gains flow to working (typically higher-income) families; non-working parents in poorer households are excluded, raising a contested effect on the income gap.

membership_note: Six fundamentals bear genuinely: the policy's primary design target is O2 (household cost relief) and O4 (enabling employment); it carries significant early-years educational implications (O7), a large fiscal footprint (O12), macro labour-supply effects (O13), and a contested distributional profile tied to the working-parent conditionality (O14).
